subject: Next steps: Discovery recap, success metrics & access timeline
messages:
From: Claire Wu <claire.wu@orionhealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.p@orionhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from our discovery — where the pain is and pilot ask

Mina — thanks again for the call this morning. Wanted to capture the three things we discussed so we stay aligned before we scope a pilot:

1) Pain points
- Current latency spikes on batch inference cause delays in clinician workflow (up to 2.5s additional per request during peak).
- Model cost is unpredictable across the three environments we support (on-prem, hybrid cloud).
- Lack of granular observability makes it hard to roll back bad model versions quickly.

2) Goals for a 6‑week pilot
- Reduce median inference latency for our triage endpoint from 450ms to <250ms at p95 under simulated peak.
- Demonstrate predictable token-level cost for 100k monthly queries.
- Implement a small eval suite (10 prompt templates + 200 examples) to detect regressions.

3) Stakeholders & constraints
- Samir (eng) owns infra/credentials. I own product/metrics and will be primary point of contact for success criteria.
- Security: we need KMS integration and an audit log for token usage. Compliance team will review.

Next asks from our side:
- Can you share a short scope doc + access matrix so Samir can provision a staging VPC connection and service account?
- We’d like a proposed sprint plan and list of Redwood owners (eng + CS) for the pilot.

Thanks — Claire

--
Claire Wu
Director, Product Management
Orion Health
claire.wu@orionhealth.com

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@orionhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from our discovery — where the pain is and pilot ask

Hi Claire — great to meet you and Samir earlier. Appreciate the clear goals; I’m summarizing the pilot charter and next steps below and attaching a first draft scope and access matrix.

Pilot charter (6 weeks) — summary
- Scope: triage endpoint (JSON payload, 512-token windows), staging VPC, RBAC service account for sampling and tracing.
- Success metrics: median latency <250ms, p95 <400ms under 75% simulated load; cost predictability demonstrated via token-level forecast within +/-15% for test load; regression detection via the eval suite (10 templates x 200 examples).
- Owners: Mina (customer success / program lead), Karthik (runtime/infra lead), Olga (prompt & eval lead), Claire (product), Samir (customer infra).
- Timeline: Week 0 (access + telemetry), Week 1–2 (baseline measurement + model instrument), Week 3–4 (optimization: batching/quantization), Week 5 (evals + stability), Week 6 (readout + decision).

Access requests (attached): access_matrix.xlsx — lists required ports, KMS thumbprint, sample SAML metadata, and service account scope. Quick note on security: we can support customer-managed KMS and will provide audit logs to your compliance S3 bucket.

Attachments: redwood_poc_scope_v1.pdf (pilot scope & assumptions), access_matrix.xlsx (fields Samir requested).

Next steps (action items)
- Samir: confirm staging VPC peering details and provide service account email by Friday 03/05.
- Claire: confirm the eval templates and any priority prompt signals by 03/06 so Olga can prepare the prompt suite.
- Mina/Karthik/Olga: we’ll schedule a 30m alignment call after Samir has provisioned access (propose Mon 03/08 10am PT).

If agreeable I’ll put the draft SOW and the pilot timeline into HubSpot and send invites.

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@orionhealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Wu <claire.wu@orionhealth.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from our discovery — where the pain is and pilot ask

Hi all — quick technical checklist from my side so the staging environment is ready for the runtime tests: 

1) Network & peering
- Need CIDR ranges for your staging subnet (please confirm) and a temporary NAT for outbound model downloads.

2) Service account & IAM
- Service account email and a role that allows: create/load TLS certs, write metrics to our ingestion endpoint, and access to the KMS key (we’ll provide the exact policy snippet).

3) Sample data & traffic profile
- Please share a small sample of real payloads (anonymized) or synthetic generator so we can reproduce your peak patterns. A 1k-request sample with headers will do.

4) Observability hooks
- We’ll require an endpoint for our trace sink (TLS) and permission to push spans to the tracing endpoint. If you prefer not to expose a tracing endpoint we can ship logs to an S3 bucket you control.

If Samir can drop the service account + CIDR here, I’ll turn on the initial VM pool and run a baseline test by end of day Thursday.

Regards,
Karthik
Senior Systems Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
